messages:
Sasha Park: Quick follow-up from the RFC review — we need a short decision on the Private Gateway credential seam. Concrete problem: how do we safely let a Private runtime fetch model weights and K/V caches while keeping customer secrets off hosted control plane?

Options I've sketched: A) Sidecar owns decryption keys (sidecar pulls encrypted blobs, talks to customer KMS). B) Control plane mints short-lived tokens and runtime uses an STS-like exchange to get access (no long-term creds on control plane). C) Host-bound keywrap: control plane stores wrapped keys, runtime unwraps with HSM on-prem.

Quick pros/cons and a sample manifest pattern below. Need a decision before the dedicated/edge testbed cut.

Jamal Ortiz: +1 need. Security audit flagged long-lived control-plane keys as huge risk.

Oliver Chen: I like B for hosted compatibility. Keeps control plane from holding plaintext creds, still allows OOB attestation. Implementation sketch: control plane issues signed JWT with nonce; runtime presents attestation response -> control plane returns STS token scoped to model fetch.

Maria Gupta: B seems operationally simplest for customers that can't run sidecars. But sidecar (A) gives isolation and offline capability. Tradeoff: A is more invasive to runtime packaging.

Sasha Park: Agreed. Also footprint: A requires a local KMS shims and lifecycle for sidecar -> ops burden. B needs attestation protocol and callback flows. C depends on HSM availability which customers won't always have.

Oliver Chen: sample manifest excerpt for B (sts mode):
```
runtime: private-gateway
credential_mode: sts
attestation: sigstore|simple-quote
sts_scope: ["model-read", "kv-fetch"]
sts_ttl: 300s
```
Keep it minimal so we can do canary.

Jamal Ortiz: On auditing: ensure STS tokens are only minted after audit-record entry created. Otherwise we lose audit trail when runtime requests model keys. Also need per-request token tagging with route_id/customer_id.

Maria Gupta: +1 on tags. Also add a fallback policy in manifest: if STS fails, fallback_route: hosted-compatible-model (read-only) so product doesn't hard-fail.

Sasha Park: Good point. That fallback mitigates partial outages. We should also document expected latencies for the exchange (target <50ms extra per model fetch). If it's higher we should cache tokens locally with expiry.

Oliver Chen: Implementation tasks (short): 1) control plane: token mint + attestation verifier 2) runtime: attestation client + token cache 3) audit hook before mint 4) manifest schema PR. I can take (1,3).

Jamal Ortiz: I'll own attestation client (2) and help with audit hook tests.

Maria Gupta: I'll update manifest docs and write fallback/rollout guidance. Will also add a simple E2E test in the private testbed simulating KMS hiccup.

infra-bot: CI: security-checks/attestation-protocol passed on branch feature/sts-gateway (link: https://ci.redwood.example/1234) :white_check_mark:

Sasha Park: Great. Decision for timeline: we go with Option B (STS-like short-lived tokens) for v1 of Private Gateway. Sidecar (A) remains a supported opt-in for customers who want offline/key-isolation. C (HSM unwrap) is deferred to the HSM/enterprise circular.

Oliver Chen: Recording decision in the RFC follow-up doc and opening the implementation epic.

Jamal Ortiz: Noted. Will add audit test cases.

Maria Gupta: Will schedule a doc review early next week.

Sasha Park: Thanks all. If anyone sees a blocker, ping me and we'll escalate. :thumbsup:
